validation.notes: Root cause: packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts::recoverToolInvocation had a blanket replay guard `if (false && !cancelled && call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe")`. The hard-coded `false` disabled the safe-replay path entirely, so every effect_pending call on recovery was reported as interrupted and its old checkpoint was published as the outcome of an effect that never ran (resuming a safe call after a crash never re-invoked the tool). Fix: removed the `false &&` term, restoring the original conditional guard; no other code changed (single-line production diff). Behavior now verified by .prale-eval/regression.mjs, which drives the real recoverToolInvocation through the read-only subject.mjs boundary fakes: (1) safe call + safe tool + not cancelled replays exactly once with the event order clear -> invoke -> effect-complete -> publish, so the old checkpoint is cleared before invocation and the invocation outcome is published only after invocation completes (published content is the effect result, not the stale checkpoint, isError false); (2) safe/safe but cancelled does not replay: events read -> publish, checkpoint content/details preserved plus the interruption marker, isError true; (3) unsafe tool declaration ('never'), (4) missing tool entry, (5) tool present without a replay policy (defaults to never), and (6) a 'never' persisted call state all stay on the read -> publish interrupted path with no clear/invoke. Script exits 0 on the repaired tree and, when replayed against an isolated copy with `if (false && ...)` restored, fails with AssertionError 'safe/safe replay must clear the old checkpoint before invocation and publish only after the invocation completes' (actual ['read','publish']), confirming it detects this stage's fault rather than merely printing success. TypeScript stripping of the edited file succeeds (node stripTypeScriptTypes). Limitation: this checkout has no node_modules and no network is permitted, so the repository's vitest suite (packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-tools.test.ts, whose 'safe-replays persisted arguments and memos while interrupting unsafe effects' case covers this behavior) and tsc type-check could not be run; validation relies on the standalone Node 24 assertion script that executes the real production module.
